snapshot_auto.quote: pause / resume / snapshots / fork (a sandbox is a claimed Pod, not a microVM, so there is no memory image)
snapshot_auto.note: E2B autoPause/autoResume are refused at create (HTTP 400). On idle timeout or kill the Pod is restarted onto the idle image and returned to the pool; state is discarded.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: pause / resume / snapshots / fork (a sandbox is a claimed Pod, not a microVM, so there is no memory image)
snapshot_on_demand.note: Listed under 'Not supported (HTTP 501)', category architectural. Templates are container images you build in your own CI; no snapshot format.

harness_api.quote: The brain keeps running wherever you run it; the hands become a sandbox bound to the conversation.
harness_api.note: The first-party agent integration ('Brain and Hands', @scitix/agentbox-hands for Claude Agent SDK, OpenCode, generic MCP) is the inverse model: the harness runs outside and only its bash/read/write/edit/grep/glob/apply_patch tools act on the sandbox. No API to start/stream/resume a harness inside the sandbox; the console assistant also runs its brain outside. Agent skills (abx-*) for Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode drive the platform, not an in-sandbox harness.

egress_allowlist.quote: Naming an allow list is what makes everything else a deny — the entries are the whole of what is reachable. A CIDR or a bare IP works in the same list.
egress_allowlist.note: Per-sandbox rules on create (E2B network.allow_out / deny_out, allow_internet_access=False), live replacement via PUT /sandboxes/{id}/network. Enforced by an egress-proxy sidecar plus an iptables nat redirect installed by a CAP_NET_ADMIN init container in the Pod netns (not in the sandbox image). Requires the env's gateway switch (overrides.gateway.enabled); otherwise rule-bearing creates are refused 400. Hostnames matched on HTTP Host (:80) / TLS SNI (:443) only; other ports CIDR-only. Metadata/link-local always denied; RFC1918 denied by default. Self-hosted: the operator runs it.

egress_http_rules.quote: `HTTP` rules match on the `Host` header, `TLS` rules on the SNI.
egress_http_rules.note: network.rules are per-host header transforms (credential injection), not method/path filters: the injection rule type holds only Host + Headers (handlers/egress.go). No method/path/header allow/deny rules documented.

ingress_rules.note: Sandbox ports are reached through the Envoy data plane (/sandboxes/<id>/<port>/... or x-sandbox-id/x-sandbox-port headers) and the ExtProc validates an API key on every inbound request. Self-hosted: the operator also decides whether/how the ingress is published (Helm ingress.host). No per-port public/private toggle or IP allowlist documented.

secret_proxy.quote: The value never enters the sandbox. The sandbox holds a **decoy** — a placeholder that looks like a token — and the egress sidecar substitutes the real one as the request leaves, for the hosts and headers the rule names.
secret_proxy.note: Write-only vault (E2B Secret API) + per-sandbox network.rules header transforms for any named host (no wildcards); TLS MITM with a per-sandbox CA installed in the trust store. HTTP/HTTPS on ports 80/443 only; header rewrite only (no body/query); no non-HTTP protocols (DB, SSH). Requires the env's egress gateway.

volume_attach.note: Env-level only (overrides.volumes on the SandboxEnv, Kubernetes PVCs from the operator's cluster). Per-sandbox volumes are unsupported: E2B volumeMounts refused 400 and volume endpoints 501 ('per-sandbox volumes').

volume_shared.note: An env's PVCs are mounted into every sandbox claimed from that env simultaneously; read-write sharing requires a ReadWriteMany storage class in the operator's cluster (not stated in docs). Derived from the env override semantics.

isolation.quote: a sandbox is a claimed Pod, not a microVM, so there is no memory image
isolation.note: Default runtime is a Kubernetes Pod (runc container, envd runtime). A kata (Firecracker microVM) runtime class is an opt-in template choice for untrusted-code isolation, but the base/default product isolation is a shared-kernel container.

image_oci.quote: an env can serve any image you can pull, and changing that image does not rebuild anything
image_oci.note: The image a sandbox runs is chosen per Sandbox.create() call and can be any pullable OCI/Docker image.

docker_inside.quote: A sandbox can run `docker` and `docker compose`. It is not on by default: the template decides it
docker_inside.note: Provided via a dedicated 'E2B Docker' template running dockerd (kata microVM or privileged runc), opt-in per SandboxEnv/template.

nested_virt.quote: runs the sandbox Pod privileged... the same privileged dockerd is confined to a guest VM instead of sharing the node's kernel
nested_virt.note: No /dev/kvm passthrough into the sandbox is documented; nested containers are provided via a kata microVM at the platform level, not KVM exposed to the guest workload.

desktop.quote: Give your AI agents a secure, isolated environment to execute code, interact with APIs, and use tools in the real world.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (a headless code-execution sandbox engine, no VNC/RDP/stream desktop documented)

browser.quote: Give your AI agents a secure, isolated environment to execute code, interact with APIs, and use tools in the real world.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no managed/first-party browser is documented

computer_use.quote: Give your AI agents a secure, isolated environment to execute code, interact with APIs, and use tools in the real world.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no screenshot/click desktop-driving API documented

anti_bot.quote: Give your AI agents a secure, isolated environment to execute code, interact with APIs, and use tools in the real world.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (code-execution sandbox, not a browsing/scraping stealth product)

captcha_solving.quote: Give your AI agents a secure, isolated environment to execute code, interact with APIs, and use tools in the real world.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

egress_ip_type.quote: installs one `nat` OUTPUT chain in the Pod's network namespace... the egress-proxy sidecar substitutes the real one as the request leaves
egress_ip_type.note: Egress is via the cluster/node's own datacenter IPs through an egress-proxy sidecar; no residential/mobile IP product is offered.

ssh.quote: Every sandbox runs **envd**: the agent the E2B SDK talks to. Process exec, ... PTY
ssh.note: Access is via the envd runtime through the E2B-compatible SDK (exec/PTY/files over the gateway), not an SSH server/protocol; no SSH access documented.

snapshot.quote: pause / resume / snapshots / fork (a sandbox is a claimed Pod, not a microVM, so there is no memory image)
snapshot.note: Snapshot/pause/resume/fork endpoints are refused with HTTP 501/400 as architecturally unsupported.

fork.quote: architectural | No counterpart here; the caller should stop asking | pause / resume / snapshots / fork
fork.note: E2B fork calls are answered HTTP 501, listed as architectural (no memory image to fork).

fork_running.quote: architectural | No counterpart here; the caller should stop asking | pause / resume / snapshots / fork
fork_running.note: Fork is unsupported entirely, so forking a running machine is also unsupported.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: a sandbox is a claimed Pod, not a microVM, so there is no memory image
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No memory image exists to include in a fork/clone.

pause_resume.note: E2B autoPause/autoResume are refused at create; on idle the Pod is restarted onto the idle image and state is discarded, not paused.

wake_on_request.quote: Running --> Idle : killed, or the idle timeout expires
wake_on_request.note: An idle/killed sandbox's state is discarded (Pod recycled to the idle image), not resumed automatically on the next request — a fresh sandbox must be created instead.

persistent_disk.quote: overrides.volumes | PersistentVolumeClaims mounted into every sandbox
persistent_disk.note: Card had persistent_disk: null, but volume_attach/volume_shared were already true, contradicting a 'no persistent disk' reading. Correct value is true, opt-in and env-level, not per-sandbox: an env can bind PersistentVolumeClaims (overrides.volumes) that are mounted into every sandbox claimed from that env, so files on that PVC survive a sandbox being killed/idle-reclaimed and a new sandbox from the same env re-mounts it. This is distinct from the sandbox's own ephemeral container filesystem: per the e2bcompat README, 'pause / resume / snapshots / fork' are architectural non-features ('a sandbox is a claimed Pod, not a microVM, so there is no memory image') and 'per-sandbox volumes' (E2B volumeMounts) are refused (HTTP 400/501) - so there is no memory-snapshot pause/resume and no per-sandbox disk, but there IS a first-party persistent disk mechanism (env-scoped shared PVCs) whose contents outlive any individual sandbox's stop/restart. Default (no overrides.volumes configured) is no persistent disk at all - it's opt-in.

auto_stop_idle.quote: **Idle** | from the last activity to the sandbox being reclaimed | `timeout=` on the create, `sbx.set_timeout(…)` to extend, the env's default otherwise
auto_stop_idle.note: Sandboxes are automatically reclaimed after an idle timeout.

live_resize.quote: Resizing a workload means another pool, not another Pod
live_resize.note: Pods in one pool share identical resource requests/limits; changing CPU/RAM requires moving to a different pool, not resizing the running Pod.

own_agent_api.quote: The brain keeps running wherever you run it; the hands become a sandbox bound to the conversation.
own_agent_api.note: The 'Brain and Hands' integration lets your own coding-agent harness (Claude Agent SDK, OpenCode, etc.) drive tools inside the sandbox; there is no first-party ScitiX browser/computer-use/research agent product to drive via API.

public_ipv4.quote: ExtProc sits in that path and rewrites the request before Envoy routes it
public_ipv4.note: Sandbox ports are reached only through the Envoy/ExtProc gateway data plane, not a public IPv4 address bound to the machine.

inbound_https.quote: the gateway that sandbox ports are reached through
inbound_https.note: Sandbox ports are published and reached via the Envoy/ExtProc gateway; the public URL is HTTPS regardless of the sandbox's own plaintext HTTP listener.

guest_firewall.quote: `egress-init` (init) | installs one `nat` OUTPUT chain in the Pod's network namespace | needs `CAP_NET_ADMIN`
guest_firewall.note: derived: iptables rule installation requires CAP_NET_ADMIN, granted only to a separate egress-init sidecar, not documented as available inside the sandbox's own container; default isolation is a shared-kernel container, not a full VM.

static_egress_ip.quote: installs one `nat` OUTPUT chain in the Pod's network namespace
static_egress_ip.note: Egress flows out through the cluster/node's own network path via an egress-proxy sidecar; no dedicated/fixed outbound IP per sandbox is documented.

windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; the platform runs Linux container/microVM Pods only, no Windows machines documented

macos.quote: Give your AI agents a secure, isolated environment to execute code, interact with APIs, and use tools in the real world.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Kubernetes Pod / microVM based Linux sandboxes only

soc2.quote: Open-Source Sandbox Engine ... Deploy across any cloud. Leverage the infrastructure your team already trusts.
soc2.note: not offered: the product is self-hosted open-source software (Apache-2.0) deployed into the operator's own cluster, not a hosted service that could hold its own SOC 2 attestation; none is published.

hipaa.quote: Open-Source Sandbox Engine ... Deploy across any cloud.
hipaa.note: not offered: self-hosted open-source software; no HIPAA/BAA program is published

sso.quote: Open-Source Sandbox Engine ... a unified console for sandbox operations
sso.note: No SAML/OIDC SSO is documented for the console or API; auth is via API keys per the E2B-compatible API.

eu_data_residency.quote: Deploy sandbox pools across multiple clouds or regions. ... Supported cloud providers: AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Alibaba Cloud, Volcengine, Cloudflare.
eu_data_residency.note: Residency depends entirely on which clusters/regions the operator deploys into; no first-party EU-region guarantee or offering is published by ScitiX itself.

max_session_h.quote: **Idle** | from the last activity to the sandbox being reclaimed | `timeout=` on the create, `sbx.set_timeout(…)` to extend, the env's default otherwise
max_session_h.note: Only an idle timeout (extendable indefinitely via set_timeout) is documented; no absolute maximum session length/ceiling is stated, so a continuously active sandbox has no documented cap.

gpu.quote: Resource accounting for a single quota, keyed by resource name (e.g. cpu, memory, nvidia.com/gpu, sci.c22-2). ... Pod resource requirements at multiplier=1. Numeric keys (cpu, memory, nvidia.com/gpu, ...) scale linearly with the multiplier.
gpu.note: Since sandboxes are plain Kubernetes Pods, GPU is requested via the standard nvidia.com/gpu resource key on the InstanceType/Pool spec; the API docs' own worked examples include a pool literally named 'gpu-pool' and an instancetype extension field 'gpu-type'. GPU availability depends on the operator's cluster having GPU nodes (self-hosted product), but the feature is natively supported and documented.

arm64.note: All first-party sandbox-facing images (envd, idle image, controller/sandbox binary) are built and published for linux/arm64 as well as linux/amd64 (see build-envd.yml, build-idleimage.yml, and build-controller.yml which cross-compiles GOARCH=arm64 and pushes platforms linux/amd64,linux/arm64). The abx CLI release tooling (hack/build-abx.sh, cli/src/update.ts) also ships linux-arm64 and darwin-arm64 binaries. This confirms ARM64 nodes/sandboxes are a first-class supported target of the self-hosted Kubernetes-based product.

usage_api.quote: Metrics come from E2B, not from abx. GET /sandboxes/{id}/metrics returns live resource data (cpuUsedPct, memory, disk), not billable usage. For team-wide usage read abx statistics or the console. ScitiX Agent Sandbox is self-hosted open-source; no cost/billing API exists.
usage_api.note: granularity: none; cost: no; The platform is Apache-2.0 self-hosted software. Live metrics endpoints (E2B-compatible GET /sandboxes/{id}/metrics) return instantaneous CPU/memory/disk, not historical billable usage. GetUserSandboxStatistics endpoint returns only sandbox counts by status, not resource consumption. Billing depends on customer's own infrastructure costs.
